script.title: Why The Eiffel Tower Grows Taller In Summer
script.researchSummary: The Eiffel Tower is constructed from over 7,000 tons of puddle iron, a type of wrought iron highly sensitive to temperature changes. During hot summer days in Paris, thermal expansion causes the iron atoms to vibrate more vigorously and move further apart, increasing the tower's height by up to 15 centimeters (about 6 inches).
keyFacts: The Eiffel Tower is made of puddle iron, a form of wrought iron.
Thermal expansion causes metal particles to spread apart when heated.
In peak summer heat, the tower can grow up to 15 centimeters or 6 inches taller.
Uneven sun exposure also causes the top of the tower to lean slightly away from the sun.
script.hook: Did you know the Eiffel Tower grows taller?
script.mainContent: Built from puddle iron, the massive monument reacts strongly whenever summer heat hits Paris. Thermal expansion makes its iron particles vibrate faster and spread apart, pushing it upward.
script.ending: On hot days, it actually stretches up to six inches taller.
